newsitem.title: JAPAN: LTCB to keep April prime, debenture rates unchanged.
newsitem.headline: LTCB to keep April prime, debenture rates unchanged.

text.p: The Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd (LTCB) said on Wednesday it would leave its April long-term prime lending rate at 2.5 percent, unchanged from March.
The rate is effective from April 10.
The bank also said it would set the coupon rate of its five-year debentures for sale to institutional investors at 1.9 percent in April, unchanged from those issued in March.
The LTCB is expected to officially announce its key lending and borrowing rates for April at 2 p.m. (0500 GMT).

The prime lending rate is applied to loans of one year and longer to the long-term credit bank's most creditworthy clients. The prime rate was last cut in December to a record low 2.5 percent from 2.7 percent in November.
The LTCB debenture coupon rate was last changed in February when the bank raised it to 1.9 percent from January's 1.8 percent.
Long-term prime rates in Japan are customarily set 0.9 percentage point above the coupon rate of the benchmark five-year debenture issued monthly by the Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ).
IBJ said on Tuesday it would leave its long-term prime rate for April unchanged at 2.5 percent and also leave the coupon rate for its April debenture unchanged at 1.6 percent.
